task: Review every supplied part, discover the most consequential events from the supplied evidence, cluster related reports, assign the best-fit broad news category dynamically and produce up to 150 processed stories using schema/processed-news.schema.json. The final portfolio must contain at least five well-supported stories in every category. Treat social attention as a discovery signal rather than verification. More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.summary: In May 2020, as India was preparing to overhaul its education policy, the Narendra Modi government held a review meeting on education that placed technology at the centre, to help build what the government described as a “global knowledge super power”. Two months later, the Union Cabinet approved the National Education Policy. It made digital literacy, coding and computational thinking essential skills for every student. Coding activities were proposed to begin in the middle stage (Grades 6–8), while mathematics and computational thinking had to receive stronger focus from the foundational years. In September that year, PM Modi spoke about what education should look like in the 21st century – from coding to artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, cloud computing, data science and robotics. But five years later, the latest 2025-26 UDISE+ (Unified District Information System for Education Plus) data presents a stark picture on digital awareness inside India’s schools. UDISE+ describes itself as the Ministry of Education’s official school education information system and says its data is collected from recognised schools and validated through administrative levels. items.title: Personality rights cannot be used to stifle freedom of expression, satire: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has said that it will examine whether suits seeking protection of personality rights suits are increasingly being used to prevent dissemination of information relating to a wrongdoing, or block satire or parody in the name of publicity rights [Alakh Pandey v John Doe(s) and Ors] Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani made the observation while dealing with the suit filed by Alakh Pandey, the founder of PhysicsWallah, seeking protection of his personality rights. The Bench said Pandey’s claim of personality rights in the suit may be overly broad. It stressed that the Court’s duty is to ensure that such cases are not misused for getting orders to take down legally permissible forms of expression. "In view of an earlier decision of a Coordinate Bench of this court in DM Entertainment Pvt. Ltd. vs. Baby Gift House and Others , this court would want to examine and ensure that personality rights are not deployed to prevent dissemination of information in relation to wrongdoing; or to extinguish an entire genre of expression including caricature, lampooning or parody which may not amount to commercial exploitation of an individual’s personality or publicity rights,” Justice Bh

items.title: Delhi High Court stays criminal defamation case against Sudarshan TV, Suresh Chavhanke
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently stayed the proceedings of a criminal defamation case filed against Sudarshan TV and its Chairman Suresh Chavhanke [Suresh Khanderao Chavhanke v State of NCT of Delhi & Ors] . Justice Madhu Jain said that the stay will continue till the next date of hearing of the case before the High Court on October 28. "Learned counsel for the petitioner [Chavhanke] submits that the petitioner is only an anchor of a TV Show and there was no criminal intention on the part of the petitioner... Till the next date of hearing, there shall be a stay on the Trial Court proceedings," the Court ordered. The defamation case against Chavhanke was filed by one Mohd Tufail Khan, who runs Jamia Arabia Nizami Welfare Educational Society, an NGO and madrasa providing shelter, food and education to around 70 orphans. Khan had also sued Islamic scholar Mufti Wajahat Qasmi, Sudarshan TV and Maya Chavhanke (the director of Sudarshan TV and Suresh Chavhanke's wife) and certain other persons. He alleged that Qasmi falsely accused his organisation of anti-national activities, illegal funding and brainwashing children through social media posts and television interviews in August and Septem

items.title: Karnataka State Bar Council Chairman backs Manan Kumar Mishra, rejects allegations by YR Sadasiva Reddy
items.summary: The Karnataka State Bar Council (KSBC) has condemned allegations levelled against Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra by co-chairman of the BCI and former KSBC member YR Sadasiva Reddy , calling them unfounded and fuelled by political motivations. In a press release issued on August 24, KSBC nominated Chairman Kamaraddi VD said, "While the newly elected members of the KSBC await the formal takeover of office as per BCI guidelines, myself the Chairman, as the administrator of the Karnataka State Bar Council, reiterates absolute faith and confidence in favor of Shri Manan Kumar Mishra leading the Bar Council of India." Kamaraddi Venkaraddi Devaraddi YR Sadasiva Reddy had called for Mishra's resignation on the grounds that the BCI's August 13 direction (later withdrawn) to bar NALSAR graduating students from enrolment as advocates was issued without the Council's deliberation, resolution or authorisation. items.title: Supreme Court urges Matrimony.com, Jodi365 to tie the knot and settle
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday expressed its disinclination to entertain a plea filed by Matrimony.com challenging a Madras High Court judgment restraining it from using ‘Jodii’ for its matchmaking application [ Matrimony.com Limited v FreeElective Network Private Limited ]. However, instead of dismissing the plea today, a Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe gave Matrimony.com and Jodi365 an opportunity to explore an amicable resolution. Matrimony.com offered to rename its application “Jodi Matrimony” to avoid abruptly shutting down the business and affecting its existing users. The Bench asked the parties to discuss this proposal and indicated that it would consider the matter again if they were unable to arrive at a settlement. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe The dispute arose after Matrimony.com launched its ‘Jodii’ mobile application in October 2021. FreeElective Network Private Limited, which operates the matchmaking platform Jodi365, issued a cease-and-desist notice against this move. It subsequently filed a trademark infringement and passing-off suit before the Madras High Court against Matrimony.com. FreeElective claimed that it had been using ‘Jodi365’

items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday sought the Delhi government's response to a bail plea filed by Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader and former MLA Naresh Balyan in connection with a case registered under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) [ Naresh Balyan v. State NCT of Delhi ]. A Bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta issued notice on the plea challenging the Delhi High Court’s refusal to grant Balyan bail. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta He was arrested by the Crime Branch of the Delhi Police on December 4, 2024, for his alleged links to an organised crime syndicate operated by absconding gangster Kapil Sangwan alias Nandu. The prosecution has alleged that Balyan acted as a "facilitator" for Sangwan’s syndicate by identifying extortion targets, executing sham property agreements, and orchestrating forced property sales at throwaway rates. On August 3, the Delhi High Court had denied him bail in the matter, observing that there appeared to be a discernible nexus between Balyan and the crime syndicate based on intercepted mobile conversations. items.title: Supreme Court stays Allahabad HC order for action against lawyers who fudged copy of award
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday stayed Allahabad High Court's recent order for initiation of criminal proceedings and disciplinary action against two advocates who allegedly misled the court by filing a manipulated land acquisition award mentioning higher rate of interest than the one in the original document [Shiv Kumar Mishra v Bareilly Development Authority] A Bench of Justice PK Mishra and Justice Shree Chandrashekhar also stayed the direction for lodging complaints before the Bar Council of India and the State Bar Council to seek cancellation of the advocates' licences. The interim order was passed on a petition filed by advocate Shiv Kant Mishra, one of the counsel accused of misconduct in the matter. The matter will be heard next on October 12. Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar On July 30, a Division Bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Kshitij Shailendra at Allahabad had found that advocates Shiv Kant Mishra and Krishna Kant Mishra deliberately altered the contents of the award to secure monetary benefits for their client. items.title: Cauvery water row: Supreme Court asks Tamil Nadu to approach CWMA over proportionate share
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday asked Tamil Nadu government to approach the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) with its grievance that Karnataka was not releasing the State’s proportionate share of Cauvery water. A Bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta was hearing the Tamil Nadu government's plea seeking directions to Karnataka for immediate release of its due share of water. Appearing for Tamil Nadu, the counsel submitted, "We have to receive proportionate quantity or water, that is unfortunately not happening." The Court noted that it had previously observed that Tamil Nadu appeared to have received more water than its allocated share from Karnataka. Today, it pointed out that the State had already received water in accordance with the CWMA's directions. “You have already received the water as directed by CWMA,” said the Court. However, the counsel for Tamil Nadu contended that the CWMA had not directed the release of the proportionate quantity of water that the State was required to receive. The Court then asked Tamil Nadu to approach the CWMA on the issue. The matter will be heard again on August 31. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta The dispute

items.title: Rajasthan High Court lays down rules to prevent indiscriminate freezing of bank accounts
items.summary: The Rajasthan High Court recently laid down a framework to prevent banks and investigating agencies from indiscriminately freezing entire bank accounts during cybercrime investigations. [Balaji Enterprises v. RBI] Justice Anand Sharma directed that where the amount linked to an alleged cyber fraud is identifiable, the ordinary course should be to place a lien or hold on that amount and allow the account holder to operate the remaining balance. The petitioners had challenged the freezing, debit-freezing or lien marking of their accounts following communications from various investigating agencies. In some cases, the transaction allegedly connected with cyber fraud involved amounts below ₹100, ₹1,000, ₹5,000 or ₹10,000. However, the entire bank accounts, which contained substantially larger amounts, had been frozen. The Court said that while the State has a duty to protect cyber fraud victims and prevent the dissipation of stolen funds, investigative powers are subject to constitutional standards of legality, reasonableness and proportionality. “The seriousness of cyber-crime cannot justify abandoning the safeguards which protect an innocent citizen against arbitrary State action,” t

items.title: Jammu & Kashmir High Court seeks explanation from its registry over petition revealing rape victim’s name
items.summary: The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh has sought an explanation from its registry after a petition filed before the Court disclosed the name of the rape victim/ complainant. Justice Shahzad Azeem observed that, since the petitioner had disclosed the name of the victim/complainant, it became necessary to seek an explanation from the registry as to how the petition had been entertained despite repeated directions and circulars issued from time to time regarding such disclosures. “Keeping in view the fact that the petitioner has disclosed the name of respondent No. 2 (victim/ complainant), it becomes necessary to seek explanation from the Registry as to how this petition has been entertained despite repeated directions/ circulars issued from time to time in this regard,” the High Court observed. Justice Shahzad Azeem The matter came up before the Court on August 18. After arguments for some time, the counsel appearing for the petitioner sought permission to withdraw the petition. The Court permitted the same. items.title: Whether SG, ASG or junior counsel, our order will be the same: Supreme Court rejects adjournment request
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Saturday dismissed a plea after declining to adjourn the matter merely because the Additional Solicitor General (ASG) appearing in the case was held up in another courtroom. A Bench comprising Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva made it clear that the seniority or designation of the advocate appearing made no difference to how the Court would decide a case. This was after government counsel sought adjournment in the matter, stating that ASG is on his legs in another court. "Learned ASG is held up in some other court. Please have it on Monday or Tuesday. Let him be there," the counsel said. “Whether ASG, Solicitor General, our order will be the same. It does not differ based on the advocates who appear before us. Please tell your ASG that. If Mr. Senior counsel will appear, we will pass another order? In our court, every counsel is the same,” Justice Nagarathna said. items.title: Constructive PIL: Supreme Court lauds Tamil Nadu man for pursuing plea for Railway Subway
items.summary: The Supreme Court has lauded a Tamil Nadu resident for persistently pursuing the construction of a railway subway at Vaniyambadi, describing his efforts as an instance of “constructive civic participation” [Madurai Farooq Ahmed v. Principal Secretary to Government and Others] . A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta described the petitioner's efforts as an instance of "constructive civic participation". The Court said that petitioner Madurai Farooq Ahmed had pursued the issue for several years, not for personal benefit but to secure relief for residents and commuters of Vaniyambadi. “ The appellant has demonstrated how a vigilant and bona fide citizen can, through sustained and responsible engagement with public authorities and constitutional courts, draw attention to an issue affecting the community at large. Such constructive civic participation deserves acknowledgment ,” the Court said.
